x: Cocks and Edwards soon set about putting this right and with fine runs of 7-40 and 7-53 brought the 'A' and 'B' teams to the change-over in 11th and 16th places.

Cocks was a comfortable winner of the 880 with 2:3.7, and later went out to take second spot in the quarter with 56.7. High jumper Williams leapt 5'0", a height he clears regularly, to gain second place in his event.

Heck, Miller, Thresher, Moore and Johnston are but a few knocking on the door to 1st team honours. There are also those up-and-coming lads Cocks, Hampshire and Fairclough who will be dis-placing a few old-timers before long.

In a Junior match Mitcham proved too strong for us but all praise to Cocks for his win in the 440 (50.6) and for grand supporting roles played by Redwood (4:35·7) Mead (55.8), Morrison (2:2.1) and Pottinger (19'11½") in their respective events.

TOP: Bicourt leads Fairclough, Cocks and Morrison at the half-way mark in the Junior 5 miles Championship for the "Savage" shield. CENTRE LEFT: Linstead, the holder, leads Newell and Black in the Club 10 miles Championship for the "Macher" shield.
You will see from the list of Club records shown on pages 21 & 22 that new marks have been set up by our middle-distance men Cocks, Robinson, Kerr and Gerry North.

The first of his pupils included Fairclough, Steer and Cocks, who have since proved their worth in the Senior ranks. Tom's coaching school is still going strong at Battersea Park,where he appears each Tuesday to give them their week's programme.
